facts.text: Lion Hill holds the tomb of Liu Wu, believed to be the third Chu king of the Western Han.
The Han terracotta warriors, found in 1984 about 300 m west of the tomb, are displayed in a museum of six pits with over 5,000 figures.
Wikivoyage lists the Mausoleum of the Chu Prince at 1 Bingmayong Road, Yunlong District, as Xuzhou's miniature version of Xi'an's Terracotta Warriors.

facts.text: Xuzhou Museum, founded 1959, stands on the site of one of the Qianlong Emperor's palaces at the northern foot of Yunlong Mountain.
It covers 40,000 sq m and administers the Han terracotta warriors site and three Pengcheng king tombs at Tushan.
Admission is free; address 118 Heping Road, Yunlong District.

facts.text: Yunlong Lake is a lake in southwest Xuzhou, with Yunlong Mountain on its east side.
Wikivoyage describes it as a large scenic lake in the city's southwest; free.
Xuzhou Aquarium sits on Huxin Island in the lake; the lake is open round the clock.

xuzhou-3.notes: Open lake shore, no gate per sources. Bio draft claims AAAAA rating: not confirmed by fetched sources, omit.

facts.text: Yunlong Mountain rises 142 m in southern Xuzhou with nine dragon-like peaks, 97.9% forest cover.
Setting Free Cranes Pavilion on the mountain was first built in the Northern Song.
Climb on foot or take the cable car; Yunlong Lake lies to the west.

xuzhou-4.notes: Mountain park is free; CNY 4 is only Xinghua Temple (extra inside). Cable car not counted.

facts.text: The Guishan tombs hold Liu Zhu, sixth Chu king of the Western Han (reigned 128-116 BC), and his wife.
Workmen dug out the mountainside to make a palace-like tomb of two corridors and five halls.
Address: 3 Xiangwang Road North, Gulou District.

facts.text: Hubu Hill's courtyard houses were built by Ming and Qing officials and wealthy merchants.
Two of them, the Zhai and Yu family compounds, house the Xuzhou Folk Museum (Ming and Qing daily life).
The complex sits in the centre of the city on Hubu Hill, near Ximatai.

facts.text: The museum covers the Huaihai Campaign, a major campaign of the Chinese Civil War.
It stands in a large park at 2 Jiefang Road South, Quanshan District.
Free to enter.

facts.text: The museum holds over 1,000 Han-dynasty stone sculptures, including the Weaving Picture and Cattle Ploughing Picture.
It sits on the eastern bank of Yunlong Lake in a South Hall and a North Hall that replicates Han architecture.
Chinatripedia lists the ticket as free.

facts.text: Quanshan National Forest Park covers the five peaks of Mount Quanshan on Xuzhou's southern edge, nicknamed a nature oxygen bar.
It has arboretums and China's biggest bird garden, Niaoyue Garden.

facts.text: Xuzhou Aquarium is on Huxin Island in Yunlong Lake and holds hundreds of aquatic species.
Wikivoyage calls it one of the largest aquariums in Asia.

facts.text: Mount Huaguo in Haizhou District inspired the legendary mountain in Journey to the West.
Its summit, Yunu Peak, is the highest point in Jiangsu at 625.3 m.
Shuilian Cave is the legendary home of the Monkey King, Sun Wukong.

facts.text: Lian Island is Jiangsu's largest island in Haizhou Bay, 9 km long, 80% forested.
The longest sea dyke in China links it to the mainland.
It is the only AAAA-class seashore attraction in Jiangsu.

facts.text: Yuntai Mountains are the coastal range in Lianyungang that includes Mount Huaguo.
Seaside Yuntai Mountain is a scenic area of waterfalls and peaks; ticket CNY 80 in the 20 Apr-20 Oct season.

facts.text: Kongwang Mountain is 129 m high in south Haizhou; named for the story that Confucius climbed it to look at the sea.
It holds Han-dynasty Buddhist cliff carvings among the earliest in China.
A one-hour old-road hike links the carvings and Longdongan ruins.

facts.text: Xishuang Lake in Donghai County is a 4A scenic area of 8.1 sq km, 5.39 sq km of it water, and a national wetland park.
It has a lily park, 17-arch bridge and crystal tower echoing Donghai's crystal trade.
Run by Donghai Culture and Tourism Group.
